penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A practical solution here is a setup/configuration service (delegated access, per-client credential vault, or MFA bridge guidance) that likely requires per-client manual implementation work or at minimum a guided onboarding review per org — not a fully automated delivery.

penalties_applied.name: not_legitimate_or_grey
penalties_applied.reason: Not applicable — legitimate compliance/access management problem.

rationale: The buyer is a well-defined, paying professional — Salesforce freelance admins who earn their living from multi-client consulting — so the commercial intent is real. However, the core deliverable is inherently technical infrastructure (device-agnostic MFA bridges, credential vaults, delegated Salesforce access configuration) that cannot be built and delivered autonomously by Claude + a simple web page + Stripe; it requires per-client setup work and likely vendor integrations, pulling operational_autonomy and buildability_with_ai well below their build-gate floors. The weighted total (5.8) before penalty already misses the build threshold, and after applying the human-fulfillment penalty it drops to 4.3 — below the validate floor.
solution_plan: This idea is not viable for a solo non-technical operator running an autonomous Claude factory. The problem is real and the buyers exist, but the solution is fundamentally a technical configuration service (setting up delegated Salesforce access or a per-client MFA credential workflow per org). Each client engagement requires bespoke setup that a human IT professional must execute — it is not automatable via prompts, a landing page, and a Stripe link. A non-technical operator could not build or maintain this without per-customer manual involvement, which defeats the factory model. Drop and do not pursue.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 4, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (scored 4, floor is 6). Even without the human-fulfillment penalty the total (5.8) only reaches validate range, not build range. The underlying pain is real but the solution type is incompatible with autonomous delivery.
